source: Cambodia Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF), presentation deck "ប្រព័ន្ធវប្បកម្មដំណាំស្រូវ តាមគោលការណ៍ធម្មជាតិ (ប.វ.ស)" [System of Rice Intensification Following Natural Principles (SRI)], undated PowerPoint presentation (no author, date, or elibrary URL visible on slides)
text:
Under the System of Rice Intensification (SRI), fields should be weeded and the soil surface stirred/aerated 2-4 times during the growth cycle. This weeding and soil-turning practice serves several purposes at once: it lets air circulate into the root zone, allows rice roots to grow longer/deeper, and removes weeds that would otherwise compete with the rice plant for nutrients, light, and water.

The source photos show a specific hand-pushed mechanical weeding tool with a wheel-and-tine or rotating head that a farmer pushes down the straight planted rows between hills; this tool both uproots weeds and stirs/aerates the topsoil in a single pass, which is only practical because SRI fields are planted in straight, evenly spaced rows (see the SRI transplanting technique entry). The weeded and stirred material (uprooted weeds and loosened soil) is left in the field, where it can decompose and return nutrients to the soil, similar in effect to incorporating green manure.
